propositions: When a ticket re-enters review after being blocked, a deterministic pre-check compares cited evidence anchors from the original blocking findings against the current plan material to detect if the plan remains unchanged at the cited locations.

If all matchable evidence anchors are still present verbatim in the current plan AND the description component fingerprint is unchanged, a warning is printed before review execution naming the persisting findings, but the review runs anyway (warn-only, no hard block).

Anchors that cannot be matched verbatim in the current plan are treated as unmatchable and do not trigger the warning independently; the warning fires only when at least one anchor matches old text AND all matched anchors are untouched.
The precheck records a boolean flag `precheck.cited_anchor_warning` in the sidecar metrics on every plan review to enable offline measurement of warning hit rate and predictive value.

The pre-check targets the wasted-spend residue that verdict-reuse does not catch: cases where the plan prose has not changed but unrelated changes (file impact rows, commits) cause verdict-reuse to decline and force a full re-review.
